title: Steak tacos

items: 2 cups shredded iceberg or romaine lettuce
1 cup shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese (4 oz)

steps: Pat the steak dry. In a small bowl, mix 1 Tbsp oil, the chili powder, cumin, garlic, lime zest, 1 Tbsp lime juice, salt and pepper. Rub it all over the steak and let it sit at room temperature 15–30 min.
Heat a 12-inch cast-iron skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke, about 3 min. Add the remaining 1 Tbsp oil.

Scrape the garlic bits off the steak so they don't burn. Sear 3–5 min per side without moving it, until deeply browned. Check the thickest part: 130–135°F for medium-rare, 140–145°F for medium. Skirt steak is thinner, so check it after 3 min per side.
Move the steak to a cutting board and rest 5 min.
While it rests, warm the tortillas in the skillet over medium heat 20–30 sec per side, until soft and spotted. Wrap them in a clean towel.
Find the lines (the grain) running along the steak. Slice it ¼ inch thick across those lines. Squeeze the rest of the lime juice over the slices.
Fill each tortilla with steak and top with lettuce, tomato and cheese.
tips: Slicing across the grain is what makes flank steak tender. Sliced with the grain, it turns chewy.
For more flavor, marinate up to 8 hr in the fridge. Any longer and the lime makes the meat mushy.
Sirloin works too and often costs less. Cook it to the same temperatures.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the sliced steak in a skillet over medium heat 1–2 min, just until warm, so it doesn't overcook. Store the toppings separately.
